title: Heap-fuse and allocator thresholding: investigation of gradual GPU RSS growth under continuous batching with KV cache warmup
creator: Riley Chen
description: Summary: Production nodes running continuous-batching workloads with aggressive KV cache warmup show a slow, sustained increase in GPU RSS over hours (10-30% drift) even after request volume returns to baseline. This appears correlated with: (1) high prefix reuse during warmup, (2) frequent stream ownership handoffs from the runtime batcher, and (3) cudaMallocAsync pool growth that is not reclaimed promptly. Hypothesis: allocator thresholding logic + host-side staging allocation patterns are leaving small resident heap fragments that prevent the runtime from compacting or returning memory to the CUDA pool, causing cumulative RSS drift when KV cache entries are pinned across many epochs.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a dedicated-inference node with runtime-1.24 image and default gpu allocator settings
2) Run a continuous-batching driver that ramps to 4x baseline QPS for 45 minutes using variable sequence lengths (avg 512 tokens) to trigger KV cache warmup
3) After warmup, drop QPS back to baseline and continue traffic for 3 hours
4) Observe nvidia-smi and process RSS; collect allocator traces (MALLOC_ASYNC_TRACE) and runtime allocation logs every 5 minutes
5) Repeat with allocator tuning knobs: POOL_MIN_BLOCK=4MB, POOL_MAX_BLOCK=128MB, and with stream-affinity pinned vs. unpinned
observations: - RSS rises steadily during warmup and continues a slower upward trend for hours even at baseline traffic
- cudaMallocAsync pool size increases in coarse-grained steps (power-of-two bins) with many tiny resident pages interleaved
- Host-side staging buffers (pinned host memory) spike during batch merges and do not fully release due to lingering CUDA streams holding references
- Frequent small returns to the pool appear delayed — free/return latency correlated with stream synchronization events
- KV cache keeps pointers to small per-token allocations that prevent slab coalescing under current pooling policy
experiments_run: A) Increase POOL_MAX_BLOCK -> 256MB: reduced number of pool bins but RSS still grew (slower)
B) Stream-affinity pinning: reduced staging churn but introduced latencies on tiny batches
C) Aggressive KV eviction (LRU threshold lowered): immediate RSS drop but increased tail latency on cold prefixes
D) Inserted explicit cudaStreamSynchronize at batch boundaries: allowed cudaMallocAsync to return memory faster but added ~1.8ms median latency
analysis_notes: 1) Unlike previous 'slab thrashing' bugs, fragmentation here is dominated by many small resident allocations that are windowed across stream lifetimes rather than single large unused arenas
2) The allocator's heuristic to keep recently-used mini-chunks for reuse is preventing page merging; when the KV cache pins pointers scatter across multiple bins, coalescing fails
3) cudaMallocAsync's return-to-os behavior is gated by stream callbacks; our runtime batches open transient streams which extend lifetime of freed blocks until stream completion callbacks run
4) The combination of prefix caching (long-lived small allocations) and our continuous-batcher merging policy produces many interleaved lifetimes that inhibit defragmentation
proposed_mitigations: Short term (safe): add periodic background 'stream-flush and pool-trim' task running every 15 minutes to call cudaStreamQuery + attempt pool shrink on idle streams
Short term (config): expose POOL_MIN_BLOCK and POOL_MAX_BLOCK as per-node flags and set conservative defaults for heavy-KV nodes
Medium term: implement a lightweight allocator compaction pass that coalesces adjacent free mini-chunks on the host before returning them to cudaMallocAsync bins
Medium term (runtime): change batcher to reuse a bounded set of streams instead of spawning ephemeral streams per merge to reduce cross-stream lifetime overlap
Long term: redesign KV cache allocation to use chunked per-prefix arenas (large contiguous allocations per prefix) to avoid scattering tiny allocations across bins
implementation_notes: - For pool-trim task: use cudaStreamQuery on a pinned 'cleanup' stream to avoid synchronizing application streams; ensure it is opt-in via node config
- Compaction pass must be lock-free enough to not block token emission; consider running in a low-priority background thread with exponential backoff
- Per-prefix arenas require migration plan for on-disk/serialized caches and eviction behavior in presence of multi-tenant workloads
- Metrics to add: per-bin resident pages, avg chunk lifetime histogram, stream-holding-block-count, pool-trim success rate
